This is a CRKT Pharaoh, an Allen Elishewitz design, that I bought almost 10 years ago.

This is not a high end knife (not THAT cheap either). It has a 3.625in AUS8 blade, the rest of the materials is 420J2 and glass filled nylon.

It is a button lock and is a manual opening.

I bought a custom spring some years ago and converted it into an automatic (GIF in album) . You got to lower the little red knob/switch (known as CRKT's LAWKS system) to allow the button to be pressed and the blade flies open with strength, so it's very secure. Same for closing: deppress LAWKS knob, press button and close the blade. The thumbstuds are acting as the stop pins, no signs of wear here.

No blade play at all. Which seems to indicate to me that it was built with good tolerance.

If find it to be an aesthetically pleasing knife. The blade is, IMO, remarkable for this kind of price range . Unfortunetaly, the AUS8 in bead blasted finish just loves to rust, so the knife has some nasty rust stains all over the blade . And in all honesty, I'm not a big fan of recurves or dual grind blades when it comes to practicality (but I do find them pretty).
